phase: The funnel found its groove — 6 leads in one day at $3.29 — and every one of them landed in the two states we are not papered for (day 236 AM)
headline: Good morning. Something changed yesterday, and it is the best and worst news at the same time. The $300 Plan delivered SIX leads in a single day at a $3.29 CPL — more than the whole first week produced, at roughly a third of the cost. Lifetime is now 21 leads, $186.97 of $300 spent (62%), blended CPL down to $8.90, every kill gate green, all six ads live. The campaign is working. Now the other half: all six of yesterday's leads arrived with a phone number, and all six are in California and Texas — Maria Bouza (TX), Maria Vargas, Rebecca Ryland (CA), Carol Hankins Waugh (CA), Ed Schaefer (TX), Marilyn Lucier (CA). California and Texas are precisely the two states behind b7 (your CA producer-license #) and b3 (TX telephone-solicitor registration), the two items the last ad account was banned over, and compliance is still 0/7 on day six of live dialing. The machine did not just get better — it got three times better at producing exactly the exposure we have not papered. And we still cannot tell whether any of it works: the watchdog's 5:35 PM scorecard reads "Booked calls (CRM) — no CRM source connected" and "Cost per booked call — no CRM source connected" for the seventh straight day, on the same day the AURA digest reported "0 new leads in 24h." Six leads landed; one of our own systems says zero. Two moves today, one each. Frankie: the two numbers, or the written state rule — you have not answered in writing since Aug 28, and the pile just got six deep. Chitraksh: connect a CRM source and push one lead end-to-end, because 62% of the budget is gone and the deciding metric is still a dash.
source: Reconstructed from a live Gmail sweep of hanfluxai@gmail.com through 2026-09-03T01:15Z plus the on-disk workspace. Six new lead notifications Sep 2 14:56Z→23:54Z: Maria Bouza (TX), Maria Vargas, Rebecca Ryland (CA), Carol Hankins Waugh (CA), Ed Schaefer (TX), Marilyn Lucier (CA) — all with phone numbers. Sep 2 AURA digest (15:00Z): 0 new / 4 booked / 25 SLA-breached / 30 with contact / 26 unbooked / 13% / 6-min median. AUTONOMY: this AM brief fired ON-CRON at 01:15Z with workspace access — the second consecutive AM edition and the first on-time one since the blackout; but the cofounder sweep fired 00:43Z and wrote nothing (cofounder_log.json still frozen Sep 1 16:07Z) and meeting-ingest failed again at 00:03Z ("no bridge to the Mac", 14 days stale). spotlight.title: Six new CA/TX phone numbers landed yesterday. Day six at 0/7. This is the day it stops being theoretical.
spotlight.detail: Yesterday the campaign delivered six leads and every single one is in California or Texas, every single one with a live phone number: Maria Bouza (TX), Maria Vargas, Rebecca Ryland (CA), Carol Hankins Waugh (CA), Ed Schaefer (TX), Marilyn Lucier (CA). Those two states are the whole of the compliance question — b7 is your CA producer-license # on the six live creatives and the landing page, b3 is the Texas telephone-solicitor registration, and those two are the named reasons the predecessor ad account was banned. The exposure did not creep up; it stepped up six-fold in a day. There have been no written words from you on this since Aug 28. Two acceptable end-states by tonight, both cheap: (a) send Chitraksh your NPN + CA producer-license # and start the TX registration, or (b) write one line — "we call NV/ID only until b3 and b7 are placed" — and hold to it. A seventh day of neither is the single decision in this company that can end the ad account outright.

spotlight.title: CPL just fell to $3.29 and we still cannot say whether a single lead became a call
spotlight.detail: This is the frustrating shape of yesterday: performance improved sharply — six leads at $3.29 against an $8.90 blended lifetime — and the improvement is unmeasurable. The watchdog spells it out in the same scorecard that reports the win: "Booked calls (CRM) — no CRM source connected," "Cost per booked call — no CRM source connected," and, in its own words, "CPL flatters volume — cost per booked call is the deciding metric." The Meta→CRM hourly sync has been failing since Aug 27 23:47Z and has still not been re-checked. $186.97 of $300 is gone — 62% — and the number that decides whether to double the budget or kill it has never once existed. Today: connect a CRM source, or stand up the crudest possible substitute (a sheet the booking flow writes to is enough), and push ONE of yesterday's six all the way to a booked call. One completed path converts the dash into a number while there is still budget left to act on it.

spotlight.title: Six leads arrived and our own digest said "0 new in 24h" — nobody has written down who gets called
spotlight.detail: On the same day Meta delivered six form leads, the AURA digest at 15:00Z reported "0 new leads in 24 hours" alongside 25 SLA-breached, 26 unbooked and a 13% booking rate. Two systems, two stories, same company — and the pile is now 21 people deep across CA, TX, NV, ID and NJ, including one flagged "no TCPA consent — call by hand, no AI/text" and two (Ben Garcia, Claudia Nash) with no phone number on a form whose entire premise is speed-to-lead. Three small fixes settle it: reconcile the notifier count against the watchdog and against Meta so one number is true; make phone a required field on the instant form; and do ONE written triage pass over all 21 — name, state, consent, call now or hold. Sort it once on paper and every future dial follows the rule instead of whichever notification pinged last.
